per_question.question: Which seller has the best rating?
answers:
```sql
WITH seller_orders AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT oi.seller_id, oi.order_id
  FROM order_items AS oi
  JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
),
seller_ratings AS (
  SELECT
    so.seller_id,
    AVG(r.review_score) AS average_rating
  FROM seller_orders AS so
  JOIN order_reviews AS r ON so.order_id = r.order_id
  WHERE r.review_score IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY so.seller_id
)
SELECT
  s.seller_id,
  s.seller_city,
  s.seller_state,
  sr.average_rating
FROM seller_ratings AS sr
```

per_question.question: How many new customers were there in 2018?
answers:
```sql
WITH first_order AS (
    SELECT
        c.customer_unique_id,
        MIN(o.order_purchase_timestamp) AS first_order_ts
    FROM orders AS o
    JOIN customers AS c
        ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
    GROUP BY c.customer_unique_id
)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS new_customers_2018
FROM first_order
WHERE strftime('%Y', first_order_ts) = '2018';
```

This counts unique customers whose first order was placed in 2018.
[rows]
52062

```sql
SELECT COUNT(*) AS new_customers_2018
FROM (
    SELECT
        c.customer_unique_id,
        MIN(o.order_purchase_timestamp) AS first_order_date
    FROM orders o
    JOIN customers c
        ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
    WHERE o.order_purchase_timestamp IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY c.customer_unique_id
    HAVING MIN(o.order_purchase_timestamp) >= '2018-01-01 00:00:00'
       AND MIN(o.order_purchase_timestamp) < '2019-01-01 00:00:00'
) AS first_orders;
```
